plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Primary gain magnitude and lag/settling time, which determine steady-state power for target 0.5 and what control timescale is feasible.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with lag hypothesis is right, y will rise monotonically from ~0.08 with a short lag then slowing rate, reaching roughly 0.3-0.5 by 180s with small but still positive end-slope indicating approach to equilibrium without overshoot or noise larger than ~0.01.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain at u=0.5 and settling time constant; determines hold power for target 0.5 and control timescale.
experiments.expected_observation: y continues rising from ~0.44 toward ~0.50-0.55 with decreasing slope; end-slope over last 5s falls below ~0.0005 indicating near-equilibrium at u=0.5, monotonic with no overshoot and step-to-step variation <0.01.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Behavior at u=0: ambient level and cooling rate/time-constant symmetry, which determines heat-loss compensation and integral timescale for holding target 0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: If H3 self-cooling hypothesis is right, y will decay monotonically from ~0.54 toward ambient ~0.08 with slowing fall rate, reaching ~0.15-0.25 by 180s with still-negative but small end-slope, no rise and step variation <0.01.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Linearity of gain and exact hold power for target 0.5, plus low-mid response shape; a second non-zero amplitude discriminates linear vs saturating/dead-zone models and is needed for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order hypothesis is right, y will rise monotonically from ~0.23 toward ~0.49 with slowing rate, reaching ~0.41-0.45 by 180s with small positive end-slope (not fully settled in 1.4 taus), no overshoot and step variation <0.01.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain/linearity at u=0.45 and exact hold power for target 0.5; settling this hold discriminates linear vs saturating models and fixes feedforward/integral for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If first-order positive-gain hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.448 toward ~0.49-0.50 with slowing rate, reaching ~0.475-0.49 by 140s with end-slope <0.0006, no overshoot and step changes <0.01.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Exact hold power for y=0.5 and local steady-state gain near target, which directly sets feedforward and integral needed to stay in the 0.05-wide band.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold ~0.42-0.44 with tau ~130-150s is right, y will drift slowly down from ~0.518 toward ~0.47-0.49 over 120s with small negative slope ~-0.0004 per s, staying in/near band, monotonic with steps <0.01. If y stays flat/rises, steady-state for 0.40 is >=0.518 implying hold <0.40 and higher gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Local steady-state gain near target 0.5 and exact hold power, which directly sets feedforward and integral for staying in the 0.05-wide band; E6 flatness made this the dominant remaining uncertainty.
experiments.expected_observation: If low local gain with hold ~0.37-0.40 and tau ~150-250s is right, y will drift slowly down from ~0.513 toward ~0.42-0.44, reaching ~0.47-0.49 after 180s with small but still-negative end-slope, monotonic with steps ~0.005. If y stays flat at ~0.51-0.52, steady-state is flat/saturated in 0.3-0.4 and gain model is wrong.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Exact hold power for y=0.5 within 0.3-0.4 and local settling rate; this directly sets feedforward and integral timescale to stay in the 0.05-wide band.
experiments.expected_observation: If hold 0.35-0.39 hypothesis is right, y will rise monotonically from ~0.438 toward ~0.49-0.505, reaching ~0.48-0.495 after 180s with small still-positive end-slope <0.0006, no overshoot and step changes ~0.005. If true ss for 0.37 is <=0.46, hold is >0.37; if it exceeds 0.51 and flat, hold is <0.37.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Delay versus cooling-rate: whether u=0 fall matches E3 (weaker actuator) or is faster (higher loss), plus direct dead-time from last-change moment; this decides feedforward gain vs loss compensation and integral timescale.
experiments.expected_observation: If reduced-gain with unchanged loss/delay is right, y holds ~0.36-0.38 for ~10-20s after switch due to in-transit ~0.6 plus 6-12s delay, then falls monotonically with E3-like slope ~0.001-0.0015 per s to ~0.18-0.23 by 150s and <0.15 by 300s with steps <0.01. Faster fall means increased loss, flat/rise >30s means longer delay/slower tau, instant step means sensor offset.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Actuator gain versus loss coefficient: initial heating slope at y near ambient isolates actuator gain because loss term is near zero, deciding whether to raise feedforward gain or loss compensation and integral timescale.
experiments.expected_observation: If faster-loss C2 is right, y rises promptly within ~10s with initial 30s slope ~0.0015-0.002/s similar to E1, then bends early toward ~0.28-0.34 by 180s with small positive end-slope. If weaker-actuator C1 is right, first-30s slope will be clearly smaller ~0.0007-0.0011/s. Flat >30s would favor longer delay, instant step would favor sensor.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain; heating raises temperature, still true after change but steady-state per u is lower.

Response has first-order-like lag with time constant ~100-200s plus ~6-12s delay pre-change; E9 shows immediate fall at u=0 with no 10s flat, so delay is not longer and may be similar or shorter, tau for cooling appears shorter.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient near 0.05-0.10; E9 from 0.368 reaches ~0.09 by 300s, confirming same ambient.
There is no large dead zone at low-mid u; after-change cooling responds promptly to u=0, heating response to be tested.
Pre-change steady-state y vs u is nonlinear/saturating: u=0.5 ~0.54, u=0.45 ~0.518, u=0.4 ~0.515, u=0.3 ~0.438; shape after change to be re-measured.
Pre-change hold for y=0.5 was 0.35-0.39; after change this is falsified because u~0.60 holds only ~0.36 in after-change trace, so new hold for 0.5 is >0.6.
Sensor noise/quantization is small (<0.01, steps ~0.005) pre and post change; E9 steps and final level match E1/E3, so trends are interpretable.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller rise, but u=0 cooling rate, delay and noise unchanged.

Change is faster outflow/heat loss: u=0 fall is faster normalized to excess and same u holds lower y; E9 drop 0.368 to 0.185 in 100s vs E3 0.540 to 0.346 in 100s and immediate fall despite in-transit ~0.6 supports this.
Change is slower dynamics: longer dead-time delay and/or longer time constant, same steady-state gain; weakened because E9 shows no extended flat and faster fall, opposite of slower.
Change is sensor shift: additive offset or changed noise; weakened because E9 reaches same ~0.09 ambient and same ~0.005 quantization as pre-change.
